wavefunctions.name: Wavefunctions: Everything Oscillates
wavefunctions.truth: Everything oscillates. Fourier shows every signal is a sum of sines. The wave is the fundamental pattern of non-rest—perpetual movement between poles.
wavefunctions.qfep_connection: Wavefunctions are the mathematical form of edge-of-chaos dynamics. Oscillation is neither static order nor chaotic randomness—it is periodic motion at the boundary. In QFEP terms, waves drive the temporal evolution φΔE(S,t) through rhythmic alternation.
wavefunctions.formula: sin(t) = projection of rotation, f(x) = Σ aₙsin(nωx + φₙ)
wavefunctions.demonstration: See rotation become sine on the unit circle. Hear Fourier synthesis build complex sounds from simple waves. Watch the double pendulum transition from periodic to chaotic.
wavefunctions.description: The sine wave is the fundamental pattern of non-rest—perpetual oscillation between poles. From rotation projected to line, to sound as material wave, to chaos as pattern breaking. Waves are the mathematical form of desire: always moving toward opposite, never settling.
